info.description: A standing rule that drip-feeds content: which generator to run, for which site, how often, and with what topics. The generators already exist on the job runner — a populator only decides what to call and when.

name.description: What this rule is for, in your words — e.g. 'Two smart-home buying guides a week'.

site.description: Which property the output belongs to.

jobId.description: Job on the runner to invoke, e.g. post-nxtsmart. Must match an id in its catalogue — a populator naming a job that does not exist simply never fires.

jobParams.description: Parameters passed to the job, as the runner expects them: { "category": "security-cameras", "count": 1 }. Topics come from topicQueue instead and are merged in at dispatch.

topicQueue.description: Topics still to be written, oldest first. Each run takes from the front and the entry is removed, so a run never repeats the last one. When this empties the populator idles rather than inventing topics.

topicsUsed.description: Topics already consumed. Kept so a queue can be refilled without accidentally re-commissioning something already written.

cadenceHours.description: Hours between runs. 168 is weekly, 24 daily. The tick treats this as a minimum gap, not a schedule — a missed tick delays a run rather than stacking several up.

maxPerWeek.description: Hard ceiling on runs in any rolling seven days, enforced by the tick rather than by the cadence. A cadence typo can then cost you a quiet week, not two hundred published posts.

publishMode.description: Drafts by default and deliberately: unattended publishing is how a site fills with content nobody read first.

enabled.description: Off by default. A populator only starts spending AI credit once someone turns it on.

lastRunId.description: Run id on the job runner, so a populator's output can be traced back to its log.

runsThisWeek.description: Runs in the current rolling window, recomputed by the tick from runWindowStart.
